stories.headline: SpaceX Posted Notice of a $24 Billion Supercomputer. The Governor-Elect Promised “a Ban.”
stories.deck: A gas-fired plant and “super-compute facility” on about 444 acres in Starbase. Tax breaks go before the city on Dec. 9.
stories.body:
Monday, Starbase posted notice of a Dec. 9 hearing: SpaceX proposes a “gas-fired power plant and super-compute facility” on about 444 acres, with estimated capital investment of $24 billion. The city will consider a tax abatement.

The Texas Tribune reports the land was de-annexed from Brownsville earlier this year after SpaceX offered $220 million for water and wastewater projects. Brownsville’s 90-day data-center moratorium took effect last week.

Oct. 22, Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa promised “a moratorium — a ban — on all data center approvals until laws can be passed by the Legislature to protect Texans.” She takes office Jan. 19.
stories.pull_quote: a moratorium — a ban — on all data center approvals until laws can be passed by the Legislature to protect Texans.

Hinojosa, in an Oct. 22 video posted to X: “When I am governor I will issue a moratorium — a ban — on all data center approvals until laws can be passed by the Legislature to protect Texans.” She takes office Jan. 19

stories.headline: Sunday, Jeffries Was a “Hard Yes.” Tuesday, the House Referred It 211-204.
stories.deck: Massie was the only Republican who voted to keep the Hegseth impeachment alive. Jeffries: “This is not the end of it.”
stories.body:
Sunday, on ABC’s This Week, House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries was asked if Democrats would back Rep. Thomas Massie’s impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. “I’m a hard Yes on the Hegseth resolution,” he said. “Pete Hegseth has got to go.”

Tuesday at 6:02 p.m., the House voted 211-204 to refer H. Res. 1655 to the Judiciary Committee. Republicans voted 210-1. Massie was the only Republican with the 203 Democrats who voted no. One independent voted yes.

That morning, Hegseth called it a “farce.” After the vote, Jeffries said: “This is not the end of it. It’s just the beginning.”
stories.pull_quote: I’m a hard Yes on the Hegseth resolution. … Pete Hegseth has got to go.

record.label: Roll Call 317, 6:02 p.m.: On Motion to Refer H. Res. 1655 (impeaching Peter Brian Hegseth), Passed, 211-204, 18 not voting. Republicans 210-1-0-7; Democrats 0-203-0-11; Independent 1-0-0-0

stories.headline: Musk: The Order Rate “Far Exceeds” Production. He’ll “Return Deposits for a Lot of People.”
stories.deck: The Cybertruck line shuts down in about eight months, he said, for Cybercab. “Not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported.”

Monday: “The Cybertruck order rate far exceeds our production rate. We will try to make as many as possible before shutting down the line in about 8 months, but will have to return deposits for a lot of people.”

He added that this “is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media,” but a matter of “opportunity cost.” He did not name the outlets.

stories.deck: He asked to be remembered for courage for his faith. His widow, Erika, and a growing campus movement still carry the work.
stories.body:
June 29, 2025: Charlie Kirk said he wanted to be remembered “for courage for my faith.” “The most important thing is my faith.”

He co-founded Turning Point USA in 2012 and married Erika in 2021. They had two children. On Sept. 10, 2025, he was assassinated at Utah Valley University, at 31.

Eleven days later, Erika told his memorial, “I forgive him because it was what Christ did, and it is what Charlie would do.” On Oct. 14, his 32nd birthday, President Trump awarded him the Medal of Freedom. A year later, CNN reported 1,500 college chapters, up 64 percent.

A public event should have taken one phone call to confirm.

stories.headline: JPMorgan Said It Never Debanks for Politics. Here’s What the Federal Regulator Found.
stories.deck: A bank’s CEO can say anything at a shareholder meeting. A watch list is harder to argue with.
stories.body:
May 21, 2019, JPMorgan’s shareholder meeting. Jamie Dimon: “We have not and do not debank people because of their political views.”

Oct. 14, 2026: the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency found that from 2020 to September 2025, all nine of the largest banks had such policies.

JPMorgan’s payment company flagged “MAGA, Make America Great, and America First.” An employee scrubbed “right wing” and “religious” from a nonprofit’s file.

To be fair: one bank turned away a group whose political arm endorsed only Democrats. The weight of the examples is not close.

stories.headline: Letitia James Unveils Justice System That Cuts Out the Middleman: the Facts and the Law
stories.deck: New York’s top law enforcement officer, on camera: “You don’t have to look at the facts and the law.”
stories.body:
Oct. 8, the New York attorney general debate on Spectrum News NY1. The topic was prediction markets. Republican Saritha Komatireddy, a former federal prosecutor, said she has to look at the facts and the law.

Attorney General Letitia James corrected her: “You don’t have to look at the facts and the law. All you have to do is study what they do. It is illegal in the state of New York, period.”

Asked to name a past attorney general she admires, James paused. She later named Bob Abrams.

The job is looking at the facts and the law.

stories.headline: The Boston Globe Finally Unmasked the Man Behind Mass Daily News
stories.deck: He is a software engineer. He has a laptop. Readers follow him. The Globe ran a profile.
stories.body:
Oct. 10: the Boston Globe combed through public records and named the man behind Mass Daily News. Simon Pacheco, 36, a Boston software engineer. He runs the site alone, nights and weekends.

The Globe’s case: the site is largely AI-written, and its posts attack Mayor Michelle Wu.

The Globe’s own admission: the site “has broken some news, including the arrest of a City Hall employee that the Globe subsequently reported on.”

One man and a phone beat the Globe to a City Hall arrest. The Globe responded by finding out his name.
